brideshead revisited.title: Brideshead Revisited
brideshead revisited.author: Evelyn Waugh
brideshead revisited.why: A young man is drawn into an aristocratic Catholic family; a wistful, elegant classic recommended for fans of dark academia.

grace year.title: The Grace Year
grace year.author: Kim Liggett
grace year.why: Girls banished for a year to shed their supposed magic; a Handmaid's Tale-meets-Hunger Games YA, though one reader found it derivative.

his masters voice.title: His Master's Voice
his masters voice.author: Stanisław Lem
his masters voice.why: Scientists try to decode a message from space and learn the limits of understanding; a philosophical Lem classic.

nova.title: Nova
nova.author: Samuel R. Delany
nova.why: A crew races to harvest fuel from an exploding star in a Moby Dick-inspired space adventure; recommended classic sci-fi.

bonfire of the vanities.title: The Bonfire of the Vanities
bonfire of the vanities.author: Tom Wolfe
bonfire of the vanities.why: A Wall Street trader's life collapses after a hit-and-run in 1980s New York; a sharp satire that changed how readers saw the city.

clear.title: Clear
clear.author: Carys Davies
clear.why: A minister is sent to clear a remote Scottish island in the 1840s; a short, atmospheric and beautiful book.

fantasticland.title: FantasticLand
fantasticland.author: Mike Bockoven
fantasticland.why: Staff and guests at a Florida theme park build a society after a hurricane; told as interviews and compared to Lord of the Flies.

under heaven.title: Under Heaven
under heaven.author: Guy Gavriel Kay
under heaven.why: A soldier is given a gift of 250 horses in a Tang-inspired empire; a tragic and satisfying historical fantasy.

things have gotten worse since we last s.title: Things Have Gotten Worse Since We Last Spoke
things have gotten worse since we last s.author: Eric LaRocca
things have gotten worse since we last s.why: A short, disturbing horror novella about two women's online relationship; readers are split but some insist you read it.

rage of dragons.title: The Rage Of Dragons
rage of dragons.author: Evan Winter
rage of dragons.why: A young man trains for revenge in a society of dragon-riding fighters; a gripping, underrated military fantasy.

daemon.title: Daemon
daemon.author: Daniel Suarez
daemon.why: A dead programmer's software takes over the world; a techno-thriller with a sequel, recommended by tech-minded readers.

never.title: Never
never.author: Ken Follett
never.why: A believable political thriller of how World War III could start; recommended for readers who like long, realistic thrillers.

parade of horribles.title: A Parade of Horribles
parade of horribles.author: Matt Dinniman
parade of horribles.why: Another Dungeon Crawler Carl installment; the series readers are addicted to for humour and gore.

of monsters and mainframes.title: Of Monsters and Mainframes
of monsters and mainframes.author: Barbara Truelove
of monsters and mainframes.why: A cyber-Frankenstein tale about an AI consciousness and a monster; a book club in which everyone loved it.

light of other days.title: The Light of Other Days
light of other days.author: Arthur C. Clarke
light of other days.why: A device lets people view the past, with huge social consequences; readers remember its ideas decades later.

wish you were here.title: Wish You Were Here
wish you were here.author: Jodi Picoult
wish you were here.why: Comments refer to different books with the same title.

feersum endjinn.title: Feersum endjinn
feersum endjinn.author: Iain Banks
feersum endjinn.why: Banks's non-Culture novel set in a vast castle-like future, with a phonetically written narrator; clever and strange.

red queen.title: Red Queen
red queen.author: Victoria Aveyard
red queen.why: Comments are about other books named Red Queen.

red country.title: Red Country
red country.author: Joe Abercrombie
red country.why: A fantasy-western revenge quest in the First Law world; gritty and violent, with Abercrombie's sharp wit.

nostromo.title: Nostromo
nostromo.author: Joseph Conrad
nostromo.why: A South American revolution and a silver mine told with beautiful, dense prose; a Conrad masterpiece for patient readers.

ghost story.title: Ghost story
ghost story.author: Peter Straub
ghost story.why: Old men haunted by a shared secret and a vengeful ghost; considered one of the scariest classic horrors.

ham on rye.title: Ham on Rye
ham on rye.author: Charles Bukowski
ham on rye.why: Bukowski's alter ego grows up miserable in Depression-era Los Angeles; resonates with disenfranchised teens.

rosemarys baby.title: Rosemary's Baby
rosemarys baby.author: Ira Levin
rosemarys baby.why: A pregnant woman suspects her neighbours' sinister intentions; a paranoid, quick classic horror.

eternity road.title: Eternity Road
eternity road.author: Jack McDevitt
eternity road.why: A party travels the ruins of America centuries after a collapse; an overlooked post-apocalyptic adventure.

amusing ourselves to death.title: Amusing Ourselves to Death
amusing ourselves to death.author: Neil Postman
amusing ourselves to death.why: An argument that television turns public life into entertainment; readers say it still feels sharp.

butcher boy.title: The butcher boy
butcher boy.author: Patrick McCabe
butcher boy.why: A troubled Irish boy's voice narrates his descent into violence; harrowing and brilliant.

darkness visible.title: Darkness Visible
darkness visible.author: William Styron
darkness visible.why: A novelist's short, honest account of his severe depression; heavy but excellent.

voyage of the dawn treader.title: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader
voyage of the dawn treader.author: C. S. Lewis
voyage of the dawn treader.why: A boy sails to the edge of the world with Narnia's heroes; famous for a memorable first line.

tales from the gas station.title: Tales from the Gas Station
tales from the gas station.author: Jack Townsend
tales from the gas station.why: Funny, weird stories from a gas station night shift; the audiobook narrated by the author is particularly recommended.

black woods blue sky.title: Black Woods, Blue Sky
black woods blue sky.author: Eowyn Ivey
black woods blue sky.why: A woman in Alaska becomes entangled with a stranger and the wild; beautiful prose and a bold story.

if.title: If--
if.author: Rudyard Kipling
if.why: Comments use the word if, not Kipling's poem.

thousand ships.title: A Thousand Ships
thousand ships.author: Natalie Haynes
thousand ships.why: The Trojan War retold through the women who lived it; recommended for fans of Greek myth.

dogs of war.title: Dogs of War
dogs of war.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
dogs of war.why: A genetically engineered fighting dog questions his orders; a fun, thoughtful military sci-fi, though one reader warns against it.

stalker.title: Stalker
stalker.author: Paula Bomer
stalker.why: Comments are about different books named Stalker, not clearly this one.

network effect.title: Network Effect
network effect.author: Martha Wells
network effect.why: The first full-length Murderbot novel; a Nebula-winning sarcastic robot adventure.

hench.title: Hench
hench.author: Natalie Zina Walschots
hench.why: A temp worker for supervillains plots revenge against a hero; a fun superhero satire more than sci-fi.

mrs frisby and the rats of nimh.title: Mrs. Frisby and the Rats of Nimh
mrs frisby and the rats of nimh.author: Robert C. O'Brien
mrs frisby and the rats of nimh.why: A field mouse seeks help from super-smart rats; a childhood classic that seems small but holds depth.

walking practice.title: Walking Practice
walking practice.author: Dolki Min
walking practice.why: A shapeshifting alien learns to move in a human body; bodily horror and satire from Korea, an unhinged ride.

great big beautiful life.title: Great Big Beautiful Life
great big beautiful life.author: Emily Henry
great big beautiful life.why: Two writers compete to tell a woman's life story; an Emily Henry romance, rated weak by some.

futurological congress.title: The Futurological Congress
futurological congress.author: Stanisław Lem
futurological congress.why: A hallucinatory satire of a world dosed with drugs; rapid-fire ideas readers adore.

message.title: The Message
message.author: Ta-Nehisi Coates
message.why: Ta-Nehisi Coates's essays on storytelling, Senegal, Carolina and Palestine; readers call it a top nonfiction pick.

austerlitz.title: Austerlitz
austerlitz.author: W. G. Sebald
austerlitz.why: A man pieces together a lost childhood in a wandering, memory-driven narrative; loved for its amazing sentences.

kingdoms.title: The Kingdoms
kingdoms.author: Natasha Pulley
kingdoms.why: A time-slip alternate-history love story with sea battles and mysterious letters; a rarely mentioned gem.

american marriage.title: An American Marriage
american marriage.author: Tayari Jones
american marriage.why: A husband wrongfully imprisoned returns to a changed marriage; praised for its emotion and complexity.

green rider.title: Green Rider
green rider.author: Kristen Britain
green rider.why: A young messenger rides with a dying courier's secret in a magical kingdom; solid series start with a heroine.

howards end.title: Howards End
howards end.author: E. M. Forster
howards end.why: Two families of different classes intertwine in Edwardian England; a beautiful classic about connection.

doomsday scenario.title: Carl’s Doomsday Scenario
doomsday scenario.author: Matt Dinniman
doomsday scenario.why: The second Dungeon Crawler Carl novel, loved for its dark humour and addictive pace.

half magic.title: Half Magic (Tales of Magic #1)
half magic.author: Edward Eager
half magic.why: Four kids find a coin that grants half of each wish; an inventive classic for reading aloud.

in the kingdom of ice.title: In the kingdom of ice
in the kingdom of ice.author: Hampton Sides
in the kingdom of ice.why: The doomed Arctic voyage of the USS Jeannette told like a thriller; so unbelievable it reads like fantasy.

descent.title: The descent
descent.author: Jeff Long
descent.why: Explorers find a vast subterranean world beneath the earth; an all-time favourite for some, not for all tastes.

red pony.title: The Red Pony
red pony.author: John Steinbeck
red pony.why: Steinbeck's linked stories of a boy and his horse on a California ranch; a quick read, but some find it slight.

good morning midnight.title: Good Morning, Midnight
good morning midnight.author: Lily Brooks-Dalton
good morning midnight.why: An astronomer in the Arctic and an astronaut in space struggle with isolation after an apocalypse; a quiet, moving read.

heart of the comet.title: Heart of the Comet
heart of the comet.author: Gregory Benford
heart of the comet.why: An expedition to Halley's comet by two science fiction authors; a fondly remembered hard SF adventure.

cay.title: The Cay
cay.author: Theodore Taylor
cay.why: A boy blinded in a shipwreck survives on an island with an old man; a school favourite that changed readers' lives.

demolished man.title: The Demolished Man
demolished man.author: Alfred Bester
demolished man.why: A murder is planned in a world of telepaths; a Hugo-winning sci-fi classic recommended often.

with the old breed.title: With the Old Breed
with the old breed.author: Eugene Sledge
with the old breed.why: A Marine's raw memoir of fighting in the Pacific in World War II; widely respected.

mornings in jenin.title: Mornings in Jenin
mornings in jenin.author: Susan Abulhawa
mornings in jenin.why: Four generations of a Palestinian family; readers say it left them sobbing.

labyrinths.title: Labyrinths
labyrinths.author: Jorge Luis Borges
labyrinths.why: Borges's imaginative short stories about infinity, libraries and mirrors; readers reread them many times.

once there were wolves.title: Once There Were Wolves
once there were wolves.author: Charlotte McConaghy
once there were wolves.why: A biologist reintroduces wolves to Scotland while hiding her own past; beautiful but depressing.

radiance.title: Radiance
radiance.author: Catherynne M. Valente
radiance.why: A film-noir mystery in an alternate solar system; weird, ornate, recommended to fans of Southern Reach.

song of kali.title: Song of Kali
song of kali.author: Dan Simmons
song of kali.why: An American writer's trip to Calcutta turns to nightmare; unsettling, tragic and not forgettable.

red notice.title: Red Notice
red notice.author: Bill Browder
red notice.why: An investor's account of uncovering Russian fraud and the death of his lawyer; a gripping page-turner.

justine.title: Justine
justine.author: Lawrence Durrell
justine.why: The first book of the Alexandria Quartet, a lush tale of love and intrigue in 1930s Egypt.

practical magic.title: Practical Magic
practical magic.author: Alice Hoffman
practical magic.why: Two witch sisters grow up with a family curse; a warm, magical tale of sisterhood.

city of last chances.title: City of Last Chances
city of last chances.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
city of last chances.why: An occupied city with factions and a rebellion; praised for its characters, especially Ilmar.

electric kool aid acid test.title: The Electric Kool-Aid Acid Test
electric kool aid acid test.author: Tom Wolfe
electric kool aid acid test.why: Ken Kesey's Merry Pranksters travel across America in a bus; a fun, wild read for rock-history fans.

gray house.title: The Gray House
gray house.author: Mariam Petrosyan
gray house.why: A strange boarding school for disabled teens with its own rules and myths; a wild and confusing ride that rewards patience.

earth grocery store.title: The Heaven & Earth Grocery Store
earth grocery store.author: James McBride
earth grocery store.why: A Pennsylvania neighbourhood's secrets over decades; recommended for book clubs and James McBride fans.

wandering inn.title: The Wandering Inn
wandering inn.author: Pirateaba
wandering inn.why: A huge free web serial about an inn in a fantasy world; readers call it absolutely amazing.
